[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Container and Kubernetes Security: A Technical Guide"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As organizations increasingly adopt cloud-native architectures, securing containers and Kubernetes clusters has become paramount. This tutorial covers core concepts, threat vectors, and practical mitigation strategies to harden your containerized environments."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Container Image Vulnerability Scanning"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Security begins before deployment. Container images must be scanned for known vulnerabilities in their OS packages and application dependencies. Tools like Trivy or Clair should be integrated into your CI/CD pipeline."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL my-company/my-app:v1.0.0"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Implementing Kubernetes Network Policies"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, Kubernetes pods are non-isolated and accept traffic from any source. You should enforce micro-segmentation by applying Network Policies to restrict pod-to-pod communication."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-ingress
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Pod Security Standards and Contexts"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Running containers as the root user is a critical security risk. Enforce non-root execution and drop unnecessary Linux capabilities using Security Contexts in your pod specifications."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 10001
    fsGroup: 10001
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: my-app:latest
    securityContext:
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities:
        drop:
        - ALL"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices Summary"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always use minimal base images like Distroless or Alpine to reduce the attack surface."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regularly rotate secrets and avoid storing sensitive data in plain text within ConfigMaps."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enable Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and follow the principle of least privilege for service accounts."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor cluster activity using runtime security tools like Falco to detect abnormal behavior."}]
